title: Compatibility litmus: regression sentinel for streaming + tools + structured-output
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:

Build a robust, low-flakiness regression "litmus" (a.k.a. sentinel) that exercises the Core API surface for streaming responses, tool/function calling, and structured output formats across model variants and compatibility layers. This ticket centralizes test orchestration and CI gating so that any change to the runtime, streaming path, or API contract is validated end-to-end before merge to main.

Scope:
- Golden prompt deck: curated 1,200 prompts across conversational, instruction, code, and parsing tasks (diverse token lengths and edge cases). Prompts annotated with expected structured schema and tool-call traces where applicable.
- Contracts covered: streaming chunk order/metadata, tool-call start/continue/complete lifecycle, function-typed JSON outputs with typing/validation, and fallback variants when kernels/quantization alter tokenization.
- Test vectors: positive/negative cases for function args, nested JSON outputs, partial-stream aborts, chunked function-call bodies, and KV cache warm vs cold conditions.
- Model variants: baseline open models and our pinned variants (rw-rlhf-13b, rw-rlhf-7b-quant, rw-compat-1.1), plus a small synthetic variant to simulate non-streaming-only backends.

Deliverables:
1) "litmus" harness service (pytest + orchestration scripts) that can:
   - run golden deck across models in parallel (bucketed by latency class)
   - capture and canonicalize streaming frames and tool-call events into a deterministic trace format
   - validate structured outputs against JSON schemas and fuzzy-equality for numeric tokens
2) CI jobs: nightly-regression-litmus and pre-merge-fast-litmus (subset of deck), with automatic rerun on flaky thresholds and auto-bisect hooks linking suspected commits.
3) Acceptance criteria and gating rules defined in CONFLUENCE doc and encoded in CI job: fail on >0% hard-contract violations, allow up to 0.5% transient differences with auto-flake annotation.
4) Dashboards: per-prompt historical pass rates, top failure classes, and traces linked to GitHub PRs and logs.

Test plan details:
- Golden selection process: combine historical customer prompts, internal fuzzed cases, and corpus of previously failing regressions (min 30% from production). Prompts are tagged with category, expected schema, and sensitivity level.
- Structured-output validation: JSON Schema plus custom heuristics for ordering-insensitive maps, tolerated whitespace differences, and numeric tolerance. Function-call traces validated for event ordering and bodies assembled across streaming frames.
- Streaming correctness checks: sequence numbers, chunking boundaries (no dropped bytes), metadata fields (final=true), and continuity when switching routing/fallbacks.
- Compatibility permutations: run each prompt against (streaming enabled/disabled) x (function-calls on/off) x (structured-output enforcement/lenient) x (quantized/FP16).

Implementation notes & trade-offs:
- Avoid overly strict byte-for-byte matches for streaming frames; instead canonicalize and assert semantic equivalence to reduce flakiness from kernel scheduling.
- Keep the fast-litmus subset <200 prompts to keep pre-merge jobs <12 minutes; nightly full deck can be longer and more comprehensive.
- Use a golden-trace storage bucket with TTL 90 days for postmortem and comparison.
- If CI replays are noisy due to infra variability, add an adaptive retry policy before marking a test as failed and record metadata for triage.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/API/Compat+Litmus+Spec
- Golden deck CSV & annotations: https://drive.redwood.ai/goldens/compat-litmus-1200.csv
- Harness repo and runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-litmus-runner (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-litmus-runner/pull/87)
- CI job definitions: .github/workflows/ci-litmus.yml and Jenkins job "nightly-litmus"
- Example failure dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/litmus-failures

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- pre-merge-fast-litmus job runs on PRs touching runtime/streaming/tooling and passes with zero contract violations for enabled checks.
- nightly-regression-litmus runs the full deck and creates an actionable regression ticket if pass rate for any category drops >2% week-over-week or any hard-contract violation occurs.
- New runtime changes must include updates to golden annotations when behaviour change is intentional, with clear PR justification and approver sign-off from API owners.

Runbook for failures:
- Step 1: triage via dashboard link (assign to oncall runtime/compat engineer).
- Step 2: re-run litmus with --trace to produce full frame trace and collect artifacts into the golden bucket.
- Step 3: if failure repros locally, bisect commits using our auto-bisect helper and annotate PRs.
- Step 4: for transient failures, mark as flaky and add retry/backoff adjustments or add stronger canonicalization rules.
updates: 2025-02-11: Initial spike completed. Prototype runner implemented (basic streaming canonicalizer + JSON schema validator). Pushed demo to https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-litmus-runner/pull/67.
2025-02-13: PM review (Jin Park): requested clearer gating thresholds and a fast-litmus subset for pre-merge. Added acceptance criteria and fast-litmus size target.
2025-02-15: Design review (Lina Gomez): advised on trace visualization metadata for better triage. Added trace-tags to the canonicalizer output.

2025-02-17: Flakiness analysis: initial nightly run shows 1.2% transient diff rate concentrated in long-token streaming edges. Plan: add canonicalization of time-based metadata and increase numeric tolerance for streaming chunk joins.

2025-02-18: CI infra: queued job definitions for nightly-regression-litmus and pre-merge-fast-litmus. Hooked up artifact upload to golden-trace S3 and dashboard eventing. Assigned follow-ups for flaky-case reduction (ENG-83890).
